title: JWST Detects Carbon-Bearing Molecules in Atmosphere of Exoplanet K2-18b

chunks.text: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has detected carbon-bearing molecules, including methane and carbon dioxide, in the atmosphere of exoplanet K2-18b. K2-18b is a sub-Neptune exoplanet orbiting the cool dwarf star K2-18 in its habitable zone, located approximately 120 light-years from Earth in the constellation Leo.

The spectral analysis revealed an abundance of methane and carbon dioxide alongside a scarcity of ammonia. This chemical atmospheric composition supports the hypothesis that K2-18b may possess a hydrogen-rich atmosphere above a water ocean world, classified by astronomers as a Hycean exoplanet.

Observations were conducted using JWST's Near-Infrared Spectrograph (NIRSpec) and Near-Infrared Imager and Slitless Spectrograph (NIRISS). Scientists noted potential trace signals of dimethyl sulfide (DMS), a molecule primarily produced by living phytoplankton on Earth, though further confirmation is required through follow-up spectroscopic observations.

title: Perovskite-Silicon Tandem Solar Cell Achieves World Record 34.6% Efficiency

chunks.text: Researchers at the Helmholtz-Zentrum Berlin have developed a novel perovskite-silicon tandem solar cell that achieved a certified power conversion efficiency of 34.6% in laboratory tests, setting a new world record for commercial-scale silicon tandem photovoltaic devices.

The breakthrough relies on a self-assembled monolayer of custom organic molecules engineered to minimize charge carrier recombination at the interface between the perovskite absorber layer and the top electrode, significantly boosting open-circuit voltage to 1.98 volts.

Accelerated environmental stability testing demonstrated that the encapsulated tandem cell retained 95% of its initial power output after 1,200 hours of continuous operational exposure under intense Simulated Solar Light at 65 degrees Celsius.

title: Targeted mRNA Cancer Vaccine Shows Promising Results in Phase 2 Clinical Trial

chunks.text: A personalized mRNA cancer vaccine, mRNA-4157, combined with pembrolizumab reduced the risk of tumor recurrence or death by 44% compared to pembrolizumab alone in patients with resected high-risk stage III/IV melanoma, according to Phase 2 trial data.

The therapy functions by analyzing the unique mutational signature of a patient's excised tumor sample to identify up to 34 neoantigens. Synthetic mRNA encoding these specific neoantigens is then formulated into lipid nanoparticles to prime T-cell immune responses against residual cancer cells.

Patients received up to nine doses of the individualized mRNA vaccine administered intramuscularly every three weeks over a total treatment course of approximately nine months. Mild to moderate injection site soreness and low-grade fever were the most common adverse events reported.
